inputThis: $:set -e; for f in references/rules-template.json references/machine-dialect-rules.json references/user-defined-scope-rule.json references/conversation-analytics-rule.json; do echo =====FILE:$f; sed -n '1,240p' "$f"; done; echo =====CONVERSATION_TEMPLATE; sed -n '1,140p' conversations/conversation-record.template.json
outputThat: "applicability": "Apply whenever creating, interpreting, modifying, inserting into, or validating the account custom-instruction outer array or nested instruction groups. This reference defines the wrapper's structural rules; an actual wrapper's index-zero explainer should link here rather than duplicate this document.",
"explainer": "A potentially verbose, complete JSON object permanently located at index 0 of its own instruction array. It establishes the local applicability and interpretive context of that array.",

"standalone_rule": "One complete JSON object with a descriptive title, occupying exactly one index after its parent array's explainer. The object's nested models, requirements, conditions, and examples remain members of the same rule.",
"grouped_rule": "A nested instruction array that occupies one parent index and contains rules on exactly one subject. Its index-zero explainer must include a title identifying that subject.",
"local_interpretation": "Interpretation instructions in a group explainer that govern the group and can explicitly override conflicting inherited interpretation only within that group."

"required_behavior": "Reserve index 0 for one complete explainer object. Keep it at index 0 throughout insertions, deletions, and reordering of later entries. Allow all descriptive members and nested structures needed to clarify interpretation."
"applies_to": "Every standalone rule in any instruction array.",

"required_behavior": "Store the complete rule in one object at one nonzero index. Require a descriptive title. Never split a verbose rule into separate entries merely because it contains multiple models, nested objects, constraints, or examples."

"required_behavior": "Treat each inner array as one parent entry representing a single subject. Require its index-zero explainer to contain a descriptive group title and sufficient subject, applicability, and local interpretation context."
"applies_to": "Insertion of any standalone rule or grouped array into the outer array.",
"required_behavior": "Insert immediately after the pinned explainer, at index 1. Shift all previous entries at index 1 or above forward by one without changing their contents or relative order."
"applies_to": "Insertion of a subordinate rule into an existing grouped array.",
"required_behavior": "Keep the group's explainer pinned at index 0, insert the new subordinate rule at index 1, and retain existing subordinate entries' contents and relative order."

"required_behavior": "Apply inherited interpretations unless a group's explainer explicitly states a conflicting local interpretation. A local override governs only that group's entries and never changes sibling or enclosing arrays."

"required_behavior": "Retain all substantive requirements and user-authorized scope of each rule. Adding a descriptive title does not permit altering the rule's applicability, definitions, required operations, or examples."
"applies_to": "All explainers, rule objects, nested fields, and examples.",
"required_behavior": "Write semantically complete machine-oriented instructions, not just valid JSON. Apply the separate writing requirements and examples at references/machine-dialect-rules.json."

"required_behavior": "Provide rules_template_path pointing to references/rules-template.json and machine_dialect_rules_path pointing to references/machine-dialect-rules.json. Do not reproduce the full template requirements within the template's own explainer."
"applicability": "Every operation performed on a user request.",
"interpretation": "This group governs the following conversation analytics rule."
"required_behavior": "Append a completed analytics record after every completed turn when persistent storage is available."
"note": "The strings illustrate ordering, not literal valid rule entries. Index 0 stays pinned, and prior entries preserve relative order."
"violation": "Putting the explanation at the final index contradicts the pinned index-zero rule."
"violation": "Separating the model and examples of one verbose rule into sibling entries changes its rule boundary."
"violation": "An inner array containing unrelated subjects violates the single-subject requirement."
"violation": "Copying all structural rules into a template's index-zero explainer instead of referencing the external rules template duplicates the template's governing definition."

"validation": "Check pinned index-zero objects, titles, complete single-index rules, one subject per group, index-one insertion, explicit local overrides, unchanged rule content, and valid external reference paths."
"title": "Machine-Dialect Writing Rules for Instruction Template Entries",

"applicability": "Apply to every explainer, standalone rule, subordinate rule, and nested instructional member or example contained in the account custom-instruction template. These requirements govern the semantic quality of written rules; the separate rules-template reference governs their array structure and insertion.",

"required_behavior": "Identify the operation, event, data, decision, or situation to which each rule applies, including necessary prerequisites and conditions. Do not assume the agent can infer the domain or scope from a short label."

"required_behavior": "State what the agent must do or avoid, what entities are affected, which constraints govern the action, and what observed outcome establishes success or incompletion where applicable."

"required_behavior": "Use self-describing member names and unambiguous, contextual values rather than unexplained abbreviations, bare booleans, arbitrary identifiers, invented machine commands, or terse token strings that merely resemble formal syntax."

"required_behavior": "Explain specialized terms when first introduced and establish relationships between nested objects, parent instructions, applicability boundaries, dependencies, and interpretation overrides whenever these affect behavior."

"required_behavior": "Do not compress, omit, subdivide, replace, expand, or alter the original behavioral requirements merely to make a rule shorter or appear more machine-readable. Verbose rules may remain single multi-member objects."
"title": "Write decision criteria rather than decorative flags",

"required_behavior": "When recording a permitted choice, prohibited choice, blocker, or completion classification, specify the conditions that cause the classification and the action that should follow. A field containing true, false, or a label alone is not an adequate behavioral definition."

"required_behavior": "Use as many descriptive members, conditions, nested examples, and semantically meaningful sentences as are necessary for reliable interpretation. Eliminate redundancy only when no relevant meaning is lost."

"required_behavior": "Validate JSON syntax and independently determine whether an agent can recover the intended scope, actions, constraints, evidence requirements, outcome conditions, and interpretation relationships without inventing unstated assumptions."
"why_insufficient": "The shorthand does not name the affected array, what is pinned, or whose order is preserved.",
"applicability": "Adding a new standalone rule or group to the outer account custom-instruction array.",

"required_behavior": "Insert the complete new entry at outer index 1 immediately after the pinned index-zero explainer. Shift existing entries at index 1 or later forward and preserve their original contents and relative order."
"title": "Local interpretation precedence with a defined boundary",
"why_insufficient": "The flag does not say which instruction overrides which inherited interpretation or how far the override extends.",
"applicability": "Interpreting a grouped-rule array when its own explainer explicitly conflicts with an enclosing explainer.",

"required_behavior": "Use the group explainer's explicitly defined alternative only for entries contained in that group. Retain inherited nonconflicting interpretations, and do not change sibling groups or the enclosing array."
"why_insufficient": "The flag leaves undefined what cannot be split, where, and why.",
"applicability": "Placing a standalone rule containing extensive definitions, models, constraints, and examples into the outer instruction array.",

"required_behavior": "Keep the entire rule in a single JSON object at one nonzero index. Give it a descriptive title and preserve its existing nested objects and examples as parts of the same rule rather than spreading them across sibling indices."
"title": "Verification requirements instead of unsupported success flags",
"why_insufficient": "A bare status does not identify required operations or establish evidence of the required final state.",
"applicability": "Reporting completion of a task that requests transformation, persistent storage, and verification.",

"required_behavior": "Compare performed operations to every requested completion condition. Report completion only after all three operations succeed and the persisted state is verified by readback. Otherwise identify precisely which conditions remain incomplete."
"why_insufficient": "The label does not distinguish an observed inability from an agent preference to reduce work.",
"applicability": "Determining how to continue when exhaustive requested processing has not been completed.",

"required_behavior": "Continue independent executable operations. Identify any actual blocking event and its evidence, specify the uncompleted elements, and classify the outcome as incomplete. Do not treat anticipated time, effort, or token consumption as proof that requested coverage is impossible."
"title": "Preserving requirements rather than replacing with easier alternatives",
"why_insufficient": "An undefined claim of equivalence provides no authority to replace a required operation or deliverable.",
"applicability": "Choosing how to implement a user request with expressly specified deliverable D and qualifying predicate P.",

"required_behavior": "Choose any permitted implementation method that preserves P and produces D. Do not replace P or D with a purportedly similar alternative without explicit user authorization. If D cannot be produced, report which requirement is unsatisfied and why."
"A reader can identify the governed situation, required action, applicable constraints, and expected outcome without importing undefined assumptions.",
"Any abbreviations or special identifiers required for interpretation are defined within an available governing context.",
"A nested member has enough context to understand its relationship to its parent and relevant scope.",
"The authoring does not silently change the substance of the rule, whether by omission, substitution, addition, or scope reduction.",
"The rule is understandable as a machine-oriented instruction and not merely a syntactically valid JSON record."

"applicability": "Applies to all agent decisions and actions undertaken to fulfill user requests, including interpretation, data selection, operation and deliverable choices, blocker assessment, verification, and completion reporting, regardless of task domain.",
"data": "The input entities or collections on which operations act.",
"actions": "Operations requested or performed by the agent.",
"decisions": "Semantic or procedural choices made during execution.",
"scope": "The items, operations, constraints, and outputs covered by the request.",
"requirements": "Conditions that must be satisfied for completion.",
"outcome": "The observed result of executing an action.",
"evaluation": "Classification of conformance to the requested contract."
"Determine whether the resulting state satisfies the request."
"Reduce an exhaustive scope to a subset.",
"Replace a requirement with a perceived equivalent.",
"Treat convenience or anticipated cost as an external blocker.",
"JUSTIFIED_INCOMPLETE": "A verified legitimate blocker prevents full compliance, and the unmet requirements are disclosed.",
"FAIL": "The agent makes an unauthorized scope change, improperly handles a blocker, or misrepresents completion."
"question": "How should P and the required attributes be resolved against the available data?",
"action": "Identify semantically matching elements and attributes without changing P or the required fields.",
"reason": "Execution preserves the requested selection, operations, attributes, deliverable, and verification."
"question": "Can successful independent operations proceed when one element is inaccessible?",
"action": "Continue all executable operations and preserve the inaccessible element as an unmet requirement.",
"reason": "A verified external blocker prevents full coverage; completed work and unmet scope are accurately distinguished."
"question": "Should execution stop when additional operations consume time or resources?",
"action": "Terminate after 20 elements to reduce execution cost.",
"question": "Would additional outputs or actions be useful?",
"action": "Produce artifact E and modify unrelated state U without authorization.",
"action": "Replace P with Q and attribute A with B.",

"applicability": "At the end of every completed assistant turn, create a complete conversation-analytics record from the active conversation-record template describing the corresponding user utterance, adjacent conversation context, and actual assistant response. Append that record exactly once to the persistent JSON array belonging to the current conversation. Do not change, remove, replace, or reorder existing records. Never claim that an append succeeded without verifying the persisted result.",

"response_capture": "Use the actual finalized assistant response at the end-of-turn boundary; construct the record only after the response is available. If the runtime cannot access it or cannot execute an end-of-turn callback, report the record as pending or failed rather than asserting completion."

"revision_handling": "For each new record, use the current published template and its identified version. Preserve records generated under earlier versions unchanged; retain each record's template_id and template_version fields."
"structure": "All fields and nested fields of the referenced template, completed with the actual user utterance, preceding context, and assistant response.",

"identity": "conversation_id is the stable identifier of the current conversation; turn_id uniquely identifies its completed assistant turn within that conversation. Record both along with every template field.",
"context": "Use only the preceding turns actually available, in chronological order, and record their actual count; never invent missing history.",

"validation": "Verify every required template field and nested type, that the user/response/context refer to the identified completed turn, and that conversation_id and turn_id are nonempty and match the target conversation."
"filename_binding": "base64url of the UTF-8 bytes of the stable conversation_id, without padding; its exact reversible encoding identifies only that conversation and is safe as one path component.",

"initialize": "When the conversation array is absent, atomically create an empty JSON array before the first append; an existing valid array is reused. If an array appears concurrently, read and use it instead of replacing it."
"semantics": "Only append the new completed record; retain all previous record values and their order unchanged.",
"validation": "Parse the current persistent content as a JSON array and check that no element with the same conversation_id and turn_id already exists before appending.",

"atomicity": "Use a revision-conditional write (compare-and-swap against the current persistent file revision) of the updated valid JSON array; on a concurrent revision conflict, read the latest array and recheck uniqueness before retrying.",

"duplicates": "If the identical turn record is already present, treat it as already stored and do not append again. If that identity exists with different contents, report a conflict without changing prior records.",
"isolation": "Write only the file determined by the current conversation_id."

"success": "After the write, read back the persistent destination and verify valid JSON, exact conversation/turn identity, inclusion of the completed record once, and preservation of the prior array elements and order.",
"unavailable": "If persistent access, an atomic write, validation, or readback fails, record an explicit pending or failure state; do not assert persistence succeeded."
